Your example note

This example note shows how your ideal note should look. Edit it directly or use Learn format when you want Freed to learn from your edits.

Use the example note to control:

Sections, headings, and their order
Paragraphs, bullets, and numbering
Terminology, abbreviations, writing style, and detail
Non-patient-specific boilerplate and special instructions

Add verbatim text

Use quotation marks for non-patient-specific boilerplate that belongs in every note, such as a consent statement or signature.

Freed avoids adding verbatim text that makes a patient-specific clinical claim, since applying it to every note could be unsafe. By default, such text may be omitted entirely or included only when it appears plausible for the encounter. If this makes verbatim text unreliable for your use case, combine it with a special instruction as shown under Add conditional and default text.

e.g. "Patient consented to the use of Freed to record and transcribe notes during this visit."

Subjective

John Smith, a 65-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease, hypertension, and dyslipidemia, presents for routine follow-up. He reports feeling generally well since his last visit 6 months ago. He denies chest pain, palpitations, syncope, or dyspnea with his usual activities. He occasionally experiences mild shortness of breath when climbing more than one flight of stairs, which has been unchanged for several years.

The patient reports good medication adherence and has been monitoring his blood pressure at home with readings averaging 130s/80s. He walks 30 minutes daily for exercise and follows a low-sodium diet. He reports no issues with his weekly Ozempic injections and has been administering them as prescribed.

Medical History  
- Hypertension (diagnosed 2015)  
- Dyslipidemia (diagnosed 2015)  
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus (diagnosed 2018)

Surgical History  
- Percutaneous coronary intervention with stent placement to LAD (2020)  
- Appendectomy (1985)

Medications and Supplements  
- Aspirin 81 mg PO daily  
- Atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily   
- Lisinopril 20 mg PO daily   
- Metoprolol succinate 25 mg PO twice daily   
- Metformin 1000 mg PO twice daily  
- Semaglutide (Ozempic) 1 mg SC once weekly 

Allergies  
- Penicillin (rash)

Family History  
- Father: MI at age 60, deceased at 72  
- Mother: Hypertension, deceased at 80 (stroke)  
- Brother: Type 2 diabetes

Social History  
- Tobacco: Former smoker, quit in 2019, 30 pack-year history  
- Alcohol: Occasional, 1-2 drinks per week  
- Exercise: Walks 30 minutes daily  
- Diet: Following low-sodium, diabetic diet

Review of Systems  
- General: Denies fatigue, fever, weight changes  
- Cardiovascular: Mild shortness of breath with significant exertion, denies chest pain, palpitations, orthopnea, PND, syncope, edema  
- Respiratory: Denies cough, wheezing  
- Gastrointestinal: Denies abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting  
- Neurological: Denies dizziness, headaches, focal weakness

Objective

Vital Signs  
- Blood Pressure: 132/78 mmHg  
- Heart Rate: 68 bpm  
- Respiratory Rate: 16/min  
- Weight: 185 lbs (84 kg)  
- BMI: 28.3 

Physical Examination  
- General: Well-appearing male in no apparent distress  
- HEENT: Normocephalic, atraumatic. No carotid bruits  
- Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm. Normal S1, S2. No murmurs, gallops, or rubs. No JVD  
- Respiratory: Clear to auscultation bilaterally. No wheezes, rales, or rhonchi  
- Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, non-distended. No hepatosplenomegaly  
- Extremities: No edema. Pulses 2+ and equal bilaterally

Laboratory, Imaging, and Diagnostic Test Results  
- Date: April 12, 2023  
  - Lipid Panel:  
    - Total Cholesterol: 158 mg/dL  
    - LDL: 85 mg/dL  
    - HDL: 42 mg/dL  
    - Triglycerides: 140 mg/dL  
  - HbA1c: 6.9%  
  - BMP:  
    - Glucose: 118 mg/dL  
    - Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL  
    - eGFR: 74  
    - Electrolytes: Within normal limits

- Date: May 10, 2023  
  - EKG: Normal sinus rhythm, rate 65. No ST-T wave changes. No significant change from previous

- Date: November 15, 2022  
  - Echocardiogram:  
    - LVEF: 55%  
    - Wall motion: Normal  
    - Valves: No significant abnormalities  
    - Chambers: Normal size

Assessment & Plan

65-year-old male with coronary artery disease status post PCI with stent to LAD (2020), hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, presenting for routine follow-up.

Coronary Artery Disease  
Assessment: Currently asymptomatic with stable exercise tolerance. Recent echocardiogram shows normal regional wall motion without evidence of ischemia and preserved ejection fraction of 55%. Today's EKG shows normal sinus rhythm without ischemic changes. Risk factors include hypertension, dyslipidemia, type 2 diabetes, and former smoking history. Patient remains adherent to guideline-directed medical therapy.  
Plan:  
- Continue aspirin 81 mg daily  
- Continue atorvastatin 40 mg daily  
- Continue metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily  
- Schedule exercise stress test to assess functional capacity and for surveillance  
- Encourage continued physical activity and cardiac risk factor modification  
- Follow up in 6 months with lipid panel and comprehensive metabolic panel prior to visit

Hypertension
